title: What post-training changed inside Qwen 3.5 2B
question: Where in the network do the base and instruct models part ways, and can one vector move the base model toward the instruct one?

summary.headline: biggest change at layer 22 (50%); one shift vector closes -2% of the KL gap on held-out prompts

claims.text: Post-training moves the residual stream most around layer 22: the median token's state differs from the base model's by 50% of its size there.
claims.test: descriptive: measured on every token of these prompts

claims.text: Adding one vector, the average tuned-minus-base shift at layer 22 (dose 1; made and chosen on 48 prompts, measured on 48 others), to the base model closes -2% of the next-token KL gap to the tuned model (95% CI -7% to 3%); 8 random vectors of the same size close at most 2%.
claims.test: CI lower bound beats the best random vector by 5 points, on prompts that played no part in making or choosing the vector; the ratio of mean KLs, bootstrapped over prompts

data.lens_note: shifts read through qwen3.5-2b-base's final norm and unembedding
data.interval: KL: Student t over prompts; shares: bootstrap over prompts, 95%
